subject: history
title: Founding the PRC and Consolidating Power 1949-56
welcome_lead: From Tiananmen 1949 to Korea, land reform and the First Five-Year Plan.
meta_desc: A-Level Mao's China adventure on the PRC's founding, Korean War 1950-53 and early consolidation.
final_note: You can assess how Mao secured his regime through war, terror and economic planning.

concepts.def: Proclaimed by Mao Zedong from Tiananmen Gate on 1 October 1949 after CCP victory in the civil war.
Interim constitution adopted by the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference; basis of New Democracy.
Treaty of Friendship signed 14 February 1950 with Stalin, providing Soviet loans, advisers and a security alliance.
PRC sent the People's Volunteer Army across the Yalu in October 1950; Armistice 27 July 1953.
Mass redistribution of land; 'speak bitterness' sessions; perhaps 1-2 million landlords killed.
Soviet-style heavy industry drive doubling steel output; basis of the 1954 PRC Constitution.

walkthroughs.body_html: The CCP's victory was completed at Beiping in January 1949; the PRC was proclaimed on 1 October 1949. Mao flew to Moscow in December and signed the Sino-Soviet Treaty in February 1950. New Democracy preserved a coalition with friendly bourgeoisie while the CCP took the commanding heights. The Marriage Law (May 1950) and Trade Union Law extended reform.

After MacArthur approached the Yalu, the People's Volunteer Army intervened in October 1950 under Peng Dehuai. PRC casualties exceeded 400,000. The war justified domestic mobilisation: the campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries (1950-51) executed perhaps 700,000; the Three-Antis (against bureaucracy) and Five-Antis (against capitalists) of 1951-52 followed.

The First Five-Year Plan (announced 1953, retroactive) used Soviet aid for 156 industrial projects. Steel rose from 1.3 to 5.4 million tonnes by 1957. Mutual aid teams gave way to lower cooperatives, then by 1956 to higher cooperatives covering 96% of peasant households. The 1954 PRC Constitution institutionalised the National People's Congress.

mcqs.q: Why did the Communists win the Chinese Civil War?
options: Magna Carta abolished the monarchy and created Parliament.
Mao's appeal to peasants through land reform, the discrediting of the KMT by corruption and inflation, and the disciplined organisation of the PLA — not foreign aid.
Mao won because the USSR sent the Red Army to help.
Mao won because the USA refused to support the KMT.
